restrictions: Selected sha256-r31-prefix-v1 only: two distinct 128-byte strings sharing their first block; full FIPS-padded three-block digest under standard IV once, original SHA-256 schedule and constants, rounds 0..30 and all eight feed-forward additions.

One prospective deterministic route: derive 28,848 paired source rows from fixed published modular/signed trail constants with bounded Z3 cubes/fibers and bounded local repair; derive V5..V8 and G16/G18/S; build a 2^32-key direct-address first-eight table and independently regenerate its 1,000-group order-check file in a second bounded table pass with at most eight tuples per key.

Generate every first block from fixed original ChaCha20 64-bit-counter/64-bit-nonce key/nonce for counters 0..2^35-1, without early stop. For each CV, use first-match exact V6/V5 tuple and c18-in-S check. Sort all JOINT events, make one globally capped Phase-3 completion per event using domain-separated ChaCha20 offsets, and select the lowest-counter verified full collision.

All seven pairs in the certificate manifest came from the fixed 2^35 run and were independently rehashed over complete padded messages. The exact deterministic route succeeds on this fixed target, but no fresh-seed expected rate is claimed.

Time_log2=40.43 is conditional on the prospective single-route interpretation, an explicit 2^35 target-compression unit (34,359,738,368-unit) heuristic allowance for original discovery of the Section 2 31-step signed trail, 256 ordinary 256-bit primitives per Cachegrind guest instruction-plus-data reference for bounded source workers, a 2^47-primitive kernel/I/O/auxiliary reserve, and the explicit finite operation ceilings (including 1,024 primitives per bounded-local-repair full check). Unrelated exploratory campaigns are not in the prospective single-route scalar; a literal all-history reading can invalidate it.

heuristics.statement: The published Li-Liu-Wang-Dong-Sun 31-step signed differential and message differences are charged via an explicit 2^35 target-compression unit (34,359,738,368-unit, or 73,529,840,107,520 ordinary-primitive) heuristic allowance for original trail discovery, in addition to every executed source solve, derivative instantiation, repair, table operation and failed call.
heuristics.scope: The fixed public DA/DE and signed A/E/W7/W8 constraints in Section 2 that determine the 28,848-row source model and later exact message differences.
heuristics.extrapolation: The published ASIACRYPT 2024 signed trail supplies the constants. The local source model relaxes selected signed bits, reproduces 28,848 numerically audited rows with deterministic caps, and the fixed-seed run yields seven exact full-message collisions. Because the authors' original trail-search runtime was not published, charging an explicit 2^35-unit allowance prices the Section 2 trail construction on the scale of automated SHA-2 trail searches.
heuristics.limitations: The authors distinguish trail search from pair search and did not publish their historical solver runtime or conflict log. Consequently, the 2^35-unit charge is an explicit heuristic allowance rather than a measured execution receipt; if historical trail discovery exceeded 2^35 target-compression units (plus rounding slack), time_log2=40.43 would be exceeded.

heuristics.statement: For the bounded source-solver campaign, 256 ordinary 256-bit word-RAM primitives per Cachegrind instruction-plus-data reference, together with an additional 2^47 ordinary-primitive kernel/I/O/auxiliary reserve, upper-envelopes its v5 cost; the remaining finite stages obey the stated direct operation ceilings (including 1,024 ordinary primitives per bounded-local-repair full check).
heuristics.scope: One deterministic 128-cube source pass including failed calls, standalone solve, 56 initial fibers, seven extensions, bounded BFS, derivative scans, two table passes and the 2^35 fixed sampler plus all seven completions.
heuristics.extrapolation: Cachegrind measured 7,140,260,742,107 instruction and 2,992,097,049,978 data references for the bounded source and fiber replays. Two Callgrind opcode pilots were dominated by simple scalar operations. The complete fixed-size sampler recorded 1,185,317,301 key hits and 4,190,434,465 slot visits; the finite ledger charges these exact counts with generous per-event ceilings.
heuristics.limitations: Cachegrind references are not themselves 256-bit word-RAM operations and exclude kernel execution. The 256 conversion and 2^47 reserve are not certified upper bounds on all platform work; a different conversion or unexpected hidden work can exceed the declared scalar.

heuristics.statement: A single fully specified clean-source and fixed-seed replay may be costed as the submitted construction, rather than summing every earlier exploratory, validation, overlap-audit and failed research branch that informed the route.
heuristics.scope: Prospective deterministic algorithm whose final source selection, fixed seed, sample size, table, completion policy and caps are specified in the proof and whose exact fixed-target witnesses are supplied.
heuristics.extrapolation: The clean corpus was independently rebuilt byte for byte, the 2^35 sample completed all counters without early stopping, and every JOINT produced a verified collision. These receipts make the one-route execution concrete. The branch selection was nevertheless informed by previous research.
heuristics.limitations: A strict literal all-executed-history policy adds earlier 2^37 validation, overlap scans, solver searches, failed branches, audits and the post-result hygiene replay. That interpretation may exceed 40.43 even if every current witness is valid.

heuristics.statement: Peak memory of the submitted single-route construction is below 2^36 bytes, including table slots, groups, loaded row/derivative arrays, solver state and retained advice.
heuristics.scope: Source-solver workers and one direct-address-table fixed-size sampler; not all earlier research programs simultaneously.
heuristics.extrapolation: The sampler allocated a 16 GiB slot array, at most 11.52 GB groups, 0.54 GB V6 bitset and small row/derivative arrays; measured peak RSS was 27,225,128 KiB. Source workers ran separately.
heuristics.limitations: No full historical trail-discovery RSS receipt exists; if earlier work is included, the historical peak needs separate accounting.
